newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds track bunds in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds track bunds in thin trade.

text.p: Irish bonds saw moderate levels of buying interest in afternoon trade on Friday following a nervous opening on the back of weaker German bunds but overall volumes were thin, dealers said.
"We're trading in line with bunds today, which have just about recovered towards the end of the session," a dealer said.
"But there is an end-of-the-week feeling in the market and action has dried up accordingly."
Some swap-related buying at the short end had occurred in late trade, he added.
By 1445 GMT, the 6.5 Irish bond due 2001 was up five pence at 102.70 to yield 5.75 percent, while the 8.0 percent bond due 2006 was down 15 pence at 111.35 to yield 6.31 percent.
Yields against German bunds were unchanged on Thursday's close at 137 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 85 basis points over in the 10-year.
The Irish pound and rumours of an approaching revaluation, which have preoccupied the markets in recent weeks, were not a huge factor on Friday, dealers said.
The punt clawed back some ground in early trade on Friday after plunging three pfennigs against the mark and losing a penny against sterling in late trade on Thursday.
The Irish market largely shrugged off a UK preliminary second-quarter GDP rise of 0.9 percent q/q, and 3.4 percent y/y as in line with expectations.
